title: Canada Details 100,000 Extra Permanent Residence Spaces for 2027 Applicants
excerpt: IRCC has published the pathway-by-pathway breakdown for 2027, covering Hong Kong, Ukraine, family sponsorship and humanitarian applicants already in Canada who have already applied.
body:
• Canada has detailed up to 100,000 additional permanent residence spaces for 2027 for people already in Canada who have already applied — no new application or action is required.
  • The breakdown is 32,000 for Hongkonger pathways, 18,800 for Ukraine family reunification, 45,000 for spouses and dependent children of Canadians, and 12,600 for approved-in-principle humanitarian and compassionate applicants.
  • The spaces sit on top of Canada's regular 380,000 admissions target for 2027 and are part of a wider 200,000-space TR-to-PR transition measure for 2027.
  • If you are in one of these groups, check your existing IRCC application status and keep your contact details current — IRCC says applicants do not need to take any action to be considered for faster processing.

Canada's immigration department has released the breakdown of up to 100,000 additional permanent residence admissions spaces planned for 2027, giving applicants who have waited years for a decision a clearer picture of who will be processed first.

Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) published the figures in a press release on the federal government website on November 10, 2026, according to CIC News. All of the additional spaces are for persons who are already in Canada and have already applied for permanent residence.

Who gets the additional spaces

IRCC listed four groups for this cohort. The Hongkonger pathways account for 32,000 expected admissions, and the Ukraine Family Reunification Pathway accounts for 18,800. Spouses, common-law partners and dependent children of Canadian citizens and permanent residents account for 45,000, and approved-in-principle humanitarian and compassionate applicants account for 12,600.

In its own press release on Canada.ca, IRCC said it aims in 2027 to process all remaining applications under the Hongkonger pathways and the Ukraine Family Reunification Pathway. The Hong Kong pathways closed to new applications in August 2026, and the Ukraine pathway closed to new applications in October 2024, the department said.

"Canada is building on its progress to return sustainability to our immigration system while honouring the commitments we made to those in need."

— Lena Metlege Diab, Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship

The minister added that the time-limited measure would allow Canada to deliver faster on its promises to people from Hong Kong and Ukraine, giving them certainty as they build their lives in Canada.

Part of a 200,000-space transition measure

The breakdown covers what the government calls the specific humanitarian populations cohort of the 2027 TR-to-PR transition measures announced in Budget 2026. Those measures include 200,000 additional permanent residence spaces in total, on top of the 380,000 annual target for 2027 established in the 2027–2029 Immigration Levels Plan.

The other 100,000 spaces are for in-Canada workers and their family members, to be allocated in collaboration with the provinces and territories through the Provincial Nominee Program. CIC News also noted that the transition measures sit in addition to two one-time initiatives introduced in 2026 aimed at transitioning 115,000 protected persons and 33,000 foreign workers to permanent residence over 2026–2027.

IRCC stressed that people covered by the measure are already living, working and contributing in Canada, and do not represent net new arrivals. The additional spaces are in addition to the Humanitarian and Compassionate and Other category targets in the Levels Plan and do not displace resettled refugees, the department said.

What applicants should do next

Applicants do not need to take any action to have the processing of their permanent residence applications accelerated under this initiative, according to the press release reported by CIC News. There is no new form to file and no new stream to apply to under this breakdown.

For Indian and other diaspora families in Canada, the most relevant group is the 45,000 spaces for spouses, common-law partners and dependent children of Canadian citizens and permanent residents. Families with a sponsorship application already in the system should ensure their address and contact information with IRCC are up to date and monitor their application account for requests for updated documents.

Full official details are available in the IRCC release on Canada.ca. Applicants with complex cases should seek advice from a licensed Canadian immigration consultant or lawyer before acting.
